findings.issue: The Expansive Depth Mode section lists `budgetSplit` 0.5/0.35/0.15 as one of the caps but never says what a spent band does to the nodes in it. reduce-state.cjs applyReviewFrontierBudget closes every open or active node in a band as `exhausted` with reason `budget` as soon as the band spend reaches `maxIterations * share` (3.5 of the default 7), and an unspent share only rolls down to the next band once the band holds no open node (reduce-state.cjs:1979-1986). I ran the reducer over an 8-node depth-1 frontier with maxIterations 7 and 5 depth-1 visits: the projection returned stats {total:8, open:0, answered:0, exhausted:8}, every node at `exhausted/budget`, and budget.depth1 {allotted:3.5, spent:5}. Those nodes therefore never answer, `frontierOpen` falls to 0 and no `frontier_drained` candidate can form, so the seeded depth is abandoned mid-band instead of worked. Nothing in this section (or in SKILL.md line 238's "an expansive run works its seeds only") tells the reader that a band cap closes nodes, so the account of the mode's caps is incomplete.

"A node needs one iteration per configured dimension" understates the node universe. reduce-state.cjs buildDimensionUniverse starts from the four canonical dimensions and appends the configured ones, so a node is projected `answered` only once correctness, security, traceability, maintainability and every configured custom name are covered, whatever `reviewDimensions` restricts. I ran the reducer on a config with `reviewDimensions: ["correctness","performance"]` and a node whose two iterations covered both names: the node stayed `open` with coveredDimensions [correctness, performance] and nextDimension `security`. A lineage cap sized as ceil(nodes/lineages) * configured dimensions is therefore too small whenever the configured set is narrower than the canonical four.

fix.old: A node needs one iteration per configured dimension, so 50% of each lineage's `maxIterations` should reach `ceil(nodes / lineages) * dimensions`
fix.new: A node needs one iteration per dimension in its universe, the four canonical dimensions plus any custom name, so 50% of each lineage's `maxIterations` should reach `ceil(nodes / lineages) * dimensions`

findings.issue: The mutability row (and section 2's "Created during initialization. findings.issue: The scenario says the run "names `performance` next to the four canonical dimensions". Neither the case the doc invokes nor the doc's own prompt does that: review-depth-convergence.vitest.ts writes `reviewDimensions: ['correctness', 'performance']` (line 165) and the prompt at lines 29 and 41 is `review_dimensions: correctness,performance`. The described setup therefore does not match the scenario that decides pass/fail, and an operator reading it would expect a five-dimension coverage check instead of the two the test proves.

fix.old: names `performance` next to the four canonical dimensions
